mcqs.question: Two projectiles are launched from the same point on level ground with the same initial speed. One is projected at 30° above the horizontal and the other at 45°. Which projectile travels the greater horizontal range?

options.D: Cannot be determined without the speed value

mcqs.explanation: The horizontal range R = (u² sin2θ)/g. For the same speed u, sin2θ determines the range. sin(2×30°)=sin60°=0.866, sin(2×45°)=sin90°=1. Hence the 45° launch gives the larger sin2θ and therefore the greater range. Option B is correct; the other angles give smaller or equal ranges.

mcqs.question: A projectile is launched from ground level with a speed of 20 m/s at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. What is the magnitude of its velocity when it has risen to a height equal to half of its maximum height? (Take g = 9.8 m/s²)
mcqs.explanation: Maximum height H = u² sin²θ / (2g) = 400·(0.5)²/(19.6)=5.10 m. Half of H is 2.55 m. Using energy: v² = u² – 2g·y = 400 – 2·9.8·2.55 ≈ 350.0, so v ≈ 18.7 m/s. Hence option A is correct; the other values do not satisfy the energy relation.

mcqs.question: A stone is projected with a speed of 20 m/s at an angle of 60° above the horizontal from level ground. What is the total time the stone remains in the air? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
mcqs.explanation: Time of flight T = 2u sinθ / g = 2·20·sin60° / 9.8 = 40·0.866 / 9.8 ≈ 3.5 s. Option B matches this calculation; the other options are inconsistent with the formula.

mcqs.question: A projectile is launched with a speed of 25 m/s at 37° above the horizontal. What are the horizontal and vertical components of the initial velocity?
mcqs.explanation: Horizontal component uₓ = u cosθ = 25·cos37° ≈ 25·0.798 ≈ 20 m/s. Vertical component u_y = u sinθ = 25·sin37° ≈ 25·0.601 ≈ 15 m/s. Hence option A is correct; the other options swap or ignore the trigonometric decomposition.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct Cartesian equation of the trajectory for a projectile launched from the origin with initial speed u at angle θ (neglecting air resistance)?

options.A: y = x tanθ – (g x²)/(2 u² cos²θ)
options.B: y = x tanθ + (g x²)/(2 u² cos²θ)
options.C: y = x cotθ – (g x²)/(2 u² sin²θ)

mcqs.answer: y = x tanθ – (g x²)/(2 u² cos²θ)
mcqs.explanation: Deriving from x = u cosθ·t and y = u sinθ·t – ½gt², eliminating t gives y = x tanθ – (g x²)/(2 u² cos²θ). Option A matches this result; the other forms have incorrect signs or variables.

mcqs.question: A ball is thrown horizontally from the top of a 20 m high cliff with a speed of 5 m/s. How long does it take to reach the ground? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
mcqs.explanation: For horizontal launch, vertical motion is free fall: h = ½gt² ⇒ t = √(2h/g) = √(40/9.8) ≈ 2.0 s. Option B is correct; the other times do not satisfy the free‑fall equation.

mcqs.question: A projectile is launched with a speed of 30 m/s at an angle of 45° above the horizontal. What is its maximum height? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
mcqs.explanation: Maximum height H = u² sin²θ / (2g) = 900·(0.707)² / 19.6 = 900·0.5 / 19.6 ≈ 22.96 m, rounded to 23 m. Option A matches; the other values are too high or low.

mcqs.question: A stone is projected from ground level with a speed of 40 m/s at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. What horizontal distance does it cover before landing? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
mcqs.explanation: Range R = u² sin2θ / g = 1600·sin60° / 9.8 = 1600·0.866 / 9.8 ≈ 141.4 m, rounded to 141 m. Hence option B is correct; the other distances result from incorrect use of the formula or angles.
